question: Can the existing paid front support multiple distinct persistent compromise tasks, before considering changes to task-owned acceptance, personal memory and retention?
directions: All55strictly positive integer triples summing12, divided12. Same lattice as old direction-history study; no resolution/weight scan.
scalarization: Tchebycheff max_i w_i*(f_i-z_i)/fixedScale_i. z_i=min of actual paid archive at the exact request, never future values. Zero-ideal winner counts descriptive only, cannot rescue a failed primary gate.
sampling: All original first-generationCENTER step0/24/49windows from both source seeds and both development instances, no omission or replacement.
gate: Both instances:>=4of6windows support>=8distinct objective-vector task optima and >=20of55directions with >=1%scalar loss if forced to use the best equal-weight archive point, covering both seeds. Pass permits a separately designed persistent-task protocol only; failure stops this55-direction task route without ideal/scale/weight/window tuning.
distinction: PriorDIR_CHEBY changed only personal-guide selection under unchanged PDDR/retention. CENTER_HV changed Q reward. This new hypothesis would bind target identity across generation, local search, personal progress and retention, not choose another teacher or reopen failed tie/working-pool rules. No such architecture is implemented here.
requiredControlsIfContinued: Original CENTER, one equal scalar task, nonpersistent direction assignment with the same direction marginals, and ordinary MOEA/D/MPSO-D with common representation/decoder/local budget, plus strongNSGA and four-role/share ablations.
